title: Bekhorot 2
description: The first daf of Bekhorot: a donkey that is even partly owned by a gentile has no firstborn status, why the mishna needs five cases to say so, and whether, according to Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis, one may sell a gentile the fetus of a large animal, or only its future fetuses.
topics: 🫏 Buying, selling, partnering, receiving, giving: five ways a gentile can own part of the donkey
⚖️ Why the mishna needs every case: sanctity, penalties and Rabbi Yehuda’s partnership
🐴 Avoda Zara 14b: Rabbi Yehuda permits selling a damaged animal, ben Beteira a horse
🤰 Is a fetus “damaged”? Rabbi Yehuda’s baraita, damav or dameha, and Rav Ashi’s proof
🔮 Selling only the future fetuses: confusion, or separation?
🤝 Shmuel’s father: no partnerships with a gentile, lest he swear by his idol

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי, וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי, הַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף לוֹ, וְהַמְקַבֵּל הֵימֶנּוּ, וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה — פָּטוּר מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״, אֲבָל לֹא בַּאֲחֵרִים.

a3.he: צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי תְּנָא לוֹקֵחַ — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה, אֲבָל מוֹכֵר דְּקָא מַפְקַע לַהּ מִקְּדוּשָּׁה — אֵימָא לִיקְנְסֵיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a4.he: וְהַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף לוֹ, לְמָה לִי? לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: שׁוּתָּפוּת גּוֹיִ חַיֶּיבֶת בִּבְכוֹרָה, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן דִּפְטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.

a5.he: וְהַמְקַבֵּל, לְמָה לִי? מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה.

a6.he: וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה, לְמָה לִי? אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְעִיקַּר בְּהֵמָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא, לִיקְנְסֵיהּ, דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי בִּבְהֵמָה אַחֲרִיתִי, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.

a7.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בַּשְּׁבוּרָה, בֶּן בְּתִירָא מַתִּיר בַּסּוּס.

a8.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עוּבָּר מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה? טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם דְּשָׁרֵי, מִשּׁוּם דִּשְׁבוּרָה, עוּבָּר נָמֵי שָׁבוּר הוּא. אוֹ דִלְמָא: שְׁבוּרָה לָאו הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ, אֲבָל עוּבָּר, כֵּיוָן דְּהַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ, לָאו שָׁבוּר הוּא?

a9.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי. וְלָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

a10.he: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף לוֹ, וְהַמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ, וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה, דְּלָא קָתָנֵי — הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא פְּלִיג?

a11.he: אֶלָּא — פְּלִיג, וְלָא קָתָנֵי. הָכָא נָמֵי — פְּלִיג, וְלָא קָתָנֵי.

a12.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַמְקַבֵּל בְּהֵמָה מִן הַגּוֹי וְיָלְדָה — מַעֲלִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשׇׁוְויוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן חֲצִי דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן. וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי — קוֹנְסִים אוֹתוֹ עַד עֲשָׂרָה בְּדָמָיו, וְנוֹתֵן כׇּל דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן.

b2.he: וְהָא ״דָּמָיו״ קָתָנֵי! תְּנִי ״דָּמֶיהָ״. וְהָא ״נוֹתֵן כׇּל דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן״ קָתָנֵי, וְאִי בְּהֵמָה — כֹּהֵן מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ? הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּגוֹן דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ בְּהֵמָה מְעַבַּרְתָּא לְפַטּוֹמַהּ, דְּמִיגּוֹ דְּקָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ אַבְּהֵמָה, קָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ אַעוּבָּר.

b3.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בַּשְּׁבוּרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת. הָא יְכוֹלָה לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת — אָסַר, וְהָא עוּבָּר נָמֵי כְּיָכוֹל לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת דָּמֵי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b4.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַמַּתְנִיתִין, וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי. לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בַּשְּׁבוּרָה!

b5.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — שְׁבוּרָה, לָאו הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ; עוּבָּר, הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ.

b6.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַמְקַבֵּל בְּהֵמָה מִן הַגּוֹי וְיָלְדָה — מַעֲלִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן חֲצִי דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן. וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי — קוֹנְסִין אוֹתוֹ עַד עֲשָׂרָה בְּדָמָיו, וְנוֹתֵן כׇּל דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן. מַאי לָאו אַעוּבָּר? לָא, אַבְּהֵמָה.

b7.he: וְהָא דָּמָיו קָתָנֵי! תְּנִי ״דָּמֶיהָ״. וְהָא ״נוֹתֵן כָּל דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן״ קָתָנֵי, וְאִי בְּהֵמָה — כֹּהֵן מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ? הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּגוֹן דְּיָהֵיב בְּהֵמָה מְעַבַּרְתָּא לְפַטּוֹמַהּ, דְּמִיגּוֹ דְּקָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ אַבְּהֵמָה — קָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ אַעוּבָּר.

b8.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בַּשְּׁבוּרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת. הָא יְכוֹלָה לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת — אָסוּר, וְהַאי נָמֵי כְּיָכוֹל לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת דָּמֵי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b9.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מָכַר בְּהֵמָה לְעוּבָּרֶיהָ, מַאי? תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן.

b10.he: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּרָה, דְּלָא אָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי, אֲבָל שְׁלֵמָה דְּאָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי — אָסַר.

b11.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, וּמָה שְׁבוּרָה דִּפְסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שְׁלֵמָה דְּלָא פְּסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ?

b12.he: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָסְרִי רַבָּנַן אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּרָה, דִּפְסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ, אֲבָל שְׁלֵמָה דְּלָא פְּסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ — שָׁרוּ.

b13.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא: וּמָה שְׁבוּרָה דְּלָא אָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי — אָסְרִי, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שְׁלֵמָה דְּאָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי.

b14.he: וְטַעְמָא דְרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הוּא? וְהָתַנְיָא: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מַרְבִּיעִין עָלֶיהָ וְיוֹלֶדֶת! אַלְמָא מִשּׁוּם עוּבָּרֶיהָ הוּא.

b15.he: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא דִידַן מִשּׁוּם דְּאָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי בִּבְהֵמָה, אֶלָּא אַתְּ, מַאי טַעְמָא שָׁרֵית? מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין יְכוֹלָה לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת, כְּמַאן דְּזַבְּנַהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה דָּמֵי.

b16.he: וַהֲלֹא מַרְבִּיעִין עָלֶיהָ וְיוֹלֶדֶת, וְכֵיוָן דְּמַרְבִּיעִין עָלֶיהָ וְיוֹלֶדֶת — מְשַׁהֵא לַהּ!

b17.he: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ: לִכְשֶׁתֵּלֵד, דְּלֹא מְקַבֶּלֶת זָכָר.

b18.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה, וְלָא קָתָנֵי: ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי״!

b19.he: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף לוֹ דְּלָא קָתָנֵי, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּרַשַּׁאי? וְהָא אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל: אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שׁוּתָּפוּת עִם הַגּוֹי, שֶׁמָּא יִתְחַיֵּיב לוֹ שְׁבוּעָה וְנִשְׁבָּע לוֹ בְּשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ, וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: ״לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ״!

b20.he: אֶלָּא, תְּנָא מְכִירָה, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְשׁוּתָּפוּת. הָכִי נָמֵי, תְּנָא מְכִירָה וְהוּא הַדִּין לְקַבְּלָנוּת. וּמַאי שְׁנָא מְכִירָה דְּנָקֵט? דְּעִיקָּר מְכִירָה הִיא.

b21.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַמְקַבֵּל בְּהֵמָה מִן הַגּוֹי וְיָלְדָה — מַעֲלִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשׇׁוְויוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן חֲצִי דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן. וְהַנּוֹתֵן בְּקַבָּלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי — קוֹנְסִין אוֹתוֹ עַד עֲשָׂרָה בְּדָמָיו, וְנוֹתֵן כָּל דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן.

b22.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיַּד הַגּוֹי בָּאֶמְצַע — פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.

Mishna
With regard to one who purchases the fetus of a donkey that belongs to a gentile,

notes.he: ובכור הוא ועדיין הוא במעי אמו. והאי דנקט חמור ולא נקט פרה מפרש בפירקא תנינא (לקמן בכורות יג.) דאיידי דזוטרא מילי דפטר חמור פסיק ושדי ליה וכל אינך פירקין מיירי בבכור בהמה טהורה:
notes.en: MISHNA. One who purchases the fetus of his donkey: and it is a firstborn, and it is still in its mother’s womb. And the reason it takes a donkey and not a cow is explained in the second chapter (below, Bekhorot 13a): since the matters of the firstborn donkey are few, the tanna finishes them off and puts them aside, and all the other chapters deal with the firstborn of a kosher animal.

notes.dh: מתני' הלוקח עובר חמורו של עובד כוכבים והמוכר לו
notes.he: לוקח מיפטר מבכורה משום אם שהיא של עובד כוכבים ומוכר מיפטר משום ולד של עובד כוכבים ומתרי קראי (נפקי כו' ושותפות) של עובד כוכבים פוטר בבכורה אפי' אזנו וכדאמרי' (לקמן בכורות ג.) מאי שנא בו בעינן כל בכור וליכא אמו נמי בעינן כל מקנך תזכר וליכא והא דעביד צריכותא בלוקח ומוכר ולא אמר משום דנפקי מתרי קראי משום דלא תנא תרוייהו בלוקח או מוכר ש"מ דלוקח ומוכר צריכי כדמפרש ואזיל דמלוקח לא שמעינן מוכר דהוה מצי למיתני הלוקח עובר של עובד כוכבים או האם המוכר עובר לעובד כוכבים או האם (וה"נ) משמע ממתני' דמחד קרא נפקי דקתני פטור שנא' בישראל וצ"ל דאמוכר קאי דלא איירי כולה פרשה באם אלא בעובר:
notes.en: MISHNA. One who purchases the fetus of a gentile’s donkey, and one who sells to him: the purchaser is exempt from the firstborn because of the mother, which is the gentile’s, and the seller is exempt because of the offspring, which is the gentile’s. And from two verses it is derived that a gentile’s partnership exempts from the firstborn, even [a share in] its ear, as we say below (Bekhorot 3a): What is different? In it [the offspring] we require “every firstborn” (Numbers 3:13), and that is not the case; its mother too, we require “all your livestock that is male” (Exodus 34:19), and that is not the case. And the reason the Gemara argues that the purchaser and the seller are each necessary, and does not simply say that they are derived from two verses: because the mishna does not teach both [the fetus and the mother] under the purchaser or under the seller. Learn from it that the purchaser and the seller are each needed, as it goes on to explain, since from the purchaser we would not learn the seller; for it could have taught: one who purchases the fetus of a gentile’s animal or the mother; one who sells the fetus to a gentile or the mother. [One might object that] the mishna implies they are both derived from one verse, as it teaches: “exempt, as it is stated: in Israel.” One must say that this refers to the seller, since that whole passage deals not with the mother but only with the fetus.

notes.he: יוצר ובורא המאורות צופה ומאזין עתירות חכמני להבין אמרות קנויות קדם לדורות וחזקני לפרש דקדוקי בכורות:
notes.en: [Rabbeinu Gershom opens with a prayer:] Creator and Former of the lights, who sees and listens to prayers: make me wise to understand sayings acquired of old for the generations, and strengthen me to explain the fine points of Bekhorot.

notes.he: פטר חמורו של עובד כוכבים עד שהוא במעי אמו:
notes.en: One who purchases the fetus of his donkey: the firstborn of a gentile’s donkey, while it is still in its mother’s womb.

messages.text: and one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile although he is not permitted to sell a large animal to a gentile,

notes.he: כדתניא במסכת ע"ז (ד' יד:) ובכ"מ אין מוכרין להם בהמה גסה מפני שעושה בה מלאכה בשבת:
notes.en: Although he is not permitted: as is taught in tractate Avoda Zara (14b) and in many places: one does not sell them large livestock, because the gentile does labor with it on Shabbat.

notes.he: או ישראל המוכר לעובד כוכבים עובר חמורו:
notes.en: And one who sells to him: or a Jew who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile.

notes.he: כדאמרי' במסכת ע"ז דאין מוכרין בהמה גסה לעובד כוכבי':
notes.en: Although he is not permitted: as we say in tractate Avoda Zara, that one does not sell large livestock to gentiles.

messages.text: and one who enters into a partnership with a gentile in ownership of a donkey or its fetus,

notes.he: שנותנין מעות בין שניהם וקונין בהמה:
notes.en: And one who enters into a partnership with him: where the two of them put in money between them and buy an animal.

notes.he: בת"כ פ' אמור בכור איתיה בשותפות מדכתיב בכורות בקרכם וצאנכם וא"ת תיפוק לי מדאיצטריך בישראל למעוטי שותפות של עובד כוכבים מכלל דשותפות ישראל חייב וע"ק פרק ראשית הגז (חולין קלה:) דאמר בבכורות בקרך וצאנך למה לי למעוטי שותפות עובד כוכבים והכא ממעטינן ליה מבישראל ולמאי דפרישית דאיכא תרי קראי חד בעובר וחד באם ניחא מבישראל נפיק שותפות עובר ומבקרך נפיק שותפות אם וה"ה דמפיק ליה מכל מקנך תזכר וניחא ליה לאתויי בקרך איידי דמייתי התם בקרכם וצאנכם כדאמר התם אע"ג דכתיב בקרך וצאנך ואיכא למימר דידך אין שותפות לא כתב רחמנא בקרכם ולקמן מייתי מכל מקנך משום דרשא דכל וניחא דאיצטריך בקרכם משום שותפות אם דמדאיצטריך בישראל למעוטי שותפות עובד כוכבים לא מרבינן שותפות אם בישראל דההוא בולד כתיב ואין לפרש משום דגלי קרא גבי ולד בישראל שמעינן דבקרך למעוטי שותפות עובד כוכבים אתי וקאי שפיר בישראל אכולהו דהא בכולהו דממעט שותפות עובד כוכבים פרק ראשית הגז (ג"ז שם) תרומה מדכתיב ראשית דגנך פאה מדכתיב פאת שדך מעשר מדכתיב מעשר דגנך ממעט להו אע"ג דלא כתב בישראל:
notes.en: In brief: The Sifra (Torat Kohanim, Emor) derives that the firstborn applies to a partnership [of Jews] from the plural “the firstborn of your herds and of your flocks” (Deuteronomy 12:6). Tosafot asks: why not derive it from the fact that “in Israel” was needed to exclude a partnership with a gentile, which implies that a partnership of Jews is obligated? And further: in Chullin 135b (Reishit HaGez) the Gemara says that “your herd and your flock” is needed to exclude a partnership with a gentile, whereas here it is excluded from “in Israel.” Answer: according to what Tosafot explained [in the previous note], there are two verses, one about the fetus and one about the mother. From “in Israel” we exclude a gentile’s partnership in the fetus, and from “your herd” a gentile’s partnership in the mother. The same could have been derived from “all your livestock that is male,” but in Chullin the Gemara preferred to cite “your herd” because it cites “your herds and your flocks” there, as it says: although it is written “your herd and your flock,” one might say: only what is yours, and a partnership the Merciful One did not write; [hence the plural] “your herds and your flocks.” Below (3a) it cites “all your livestock” because of the exposition of “all.” And it is well that the plural “your herds” is needed for a Jewish partnership in the mother: from “in Israel,” which excludes a gentile’s partnership, we would not include a Jewish partnership in the mother, since that verse is written about the offspring. One cannot explain instead that since the verse revealed “in Israel” regarding the offspring, we learn that “your herd” comes to exclude a gentile’s partnership and “in Israel” stands for all the mitzvot: for in all the cases in Chullin 135b where a gentile’s partnership is excluded (teruma from “the first of your grain,” pe’a from “the corner of your field,” tithe from “the tithe of your grain”) it is excluded although “in Israel” is not written there. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: או מי שנותן לעובד כוכבים חצי חמורו בשותפות:
notes.en: And one who enters into a partnership with him: or one who gives a gentile half of his donkey in partnership.

messages.text: and one who receives a donkey from a gentile in order to care for it in exchange for partnership in its offspring, and one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership,

notes.he: שהחמורה של עובד כוכבים וישראל מקבלה שיהו חולקין בוולדות אבל גוף החמורה לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: And one who receives an animal from him: where the female donkey belongs to the gentile, and the Jew receives it [to tend] on condition that they divide the offspring; but the body of the female donkey belongs to the gentile.

notes.he: מן העובד כוכבים לשמור חמורו שיהו מחצית עובריה שלו או ישראל הנותן חמורו לעובד כוכבים בקבלה שיהו הוולדות למחצה או לשליש ולרביע שלו פטור מן הבכורה:
notes.en: Or one who receives: from a gentile, to look after his donkey, so that half of its fetuses will be his; or a Jew who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership, so that the offspring will be his [the gentile’s] for a half, a third or a quarter: it is exempt from the firstborn.

messages.text: in all of these cases the donkeys are exempt from the obligations of firstborn status, i.e., they do not have firstborn status and are not redeemed, as it is stated: “I sanctified to Me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal,” indicating that the mitzva is incumbent upon the Jewish people, but not upon others. If the firstborn belongs even partially to a gentile, it does not have firstborn status.

verse.he: כִּי לִי כׇּל־בְּכוֹר בְּיוֹם הַכֹּתִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הִקְדַּשְׁתִּי לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָדָם עַד־בְּהֵמָה לִי יִהְיוּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃ {פ}
verse.en: For every such first-born is Mine: at the time that I smote every [male] first-born in the land of Egypt, I consecrated every first-born in Israel, human and animal, to Myself, to be Mine, GOD’s.

notes.he: אם אותו עובר שקנה מן העובד כוכבים או שמכר לעובד כוכבים בכור הוא אינו קדוש הואיל ויש חלק לעובד כוכבים בו או באמו:
notes.en: Is exempt from the firstborn: if that fetus that he bought from the gentile, or that he sold to the gentile, is a firstborn, it is not sanctified, since the gentile has a share in it or in its mother.

notes.he: (במדבר ג׳:י״ג) הקדשתי לי כל בכור בישראל אבל לא באחרים עובדי כוכבים:
notes.en: As it is stated: “I sanctified to Me every firstborn in Israel” (Numbers 3:13), but not among others, gentiles.

notes.dh: שנאמר הקדשתי לי כל בכור בישראל
notes.he: כלומר שיהא כולו מישראל שלא יהא לעובד כוכבים חלק בו. ומפרש באידך פירקא מאי אריא דתני עובר חמורו ברישא והדר תני עובר פרתו ליתני עובר פרה ברישא וכו':
notes.en: As it is stated: “I sanctified to Me every firstborn in Israel”: that is to say, it must be entirely from a Jew, so that a gentile has no share in it. And the Gemara explains in the other chapter: why does the tanna teach the fetus of his donkey first, and then teach the fetus of his cow? Let it teach the fetus of a cow first, etc.

messages.caption: The mishna’s five cases: in each, a gentile owns the mother, the fetus, or a share of one of them.

messages.text: Gemara
Why do I need all these examples in the mishna to demonstrate the principle that a firstborn donkey must belong exclusively to a Jew for the obligations of firstborn status to apply?
messages.quote: in all of these cases the donkeys are exempt

notes.he: הלוקח והמוכר והמשתתף והמקבל והנותן:
notes.en: Why do I need all these: the purchaser, the seller, the one who enters a partnership, the one who receives and the one who gives.

messages.text: All of these examples are necessary. As, had the tanna taught that a donkey is exempt from the obligations of firstborn status only in the case where a Jew purchases a fetus from a gentile, I would say that this is because the Jew brings it to a state of sanctity in that it will not be worked on Shabbat.

notes.he: שתהא שובתת בשבת וכיון דמצוה עביד ליכא למיקנסיה:
notes.en: GEMARA. He brings it to sanctity: that it will rest on Shabbat; and since he is performing a mitzva, there is no reason to penalize him.

notes.he: פ"ה שתהא שובתת בשבת וכן מפקע לה מקדושה שהעובד כוכבים עושה בה מלאכה בשבת ולשון קדושה לא משמע כן אלא קדושת בכורה כההיא דרב מרי בר רחל דכלו חיותיה משום דמפקע להו מקדושה דהוה מקני אודנייהו לעובד כוכבים ואע"ג דבלוקח אם הולד זכר לא שייך מייתי ליה לקדושה פעמים שהעובר נקבה ומייתי לה לקדושת בכורה שולד עובר קדוש בבכורה ובלא טעם דמייתי לקדושה מצי למימר דלא שייך למיקנסיה כיון דליכא הפקעה ולא דמי למוכר דאיכא הפקעה אלא ניחא ליה למימר דאפילו הבאת קדושה איכא ועוד מצי למימר טעם אחר אי תנא לוקח משום דלא עבד איסורא אבל מוכר דעבד איסורא כדקתני אע"פ שאינו רשאי אימא לקנסיה וחד מתרי טעמי נקט ומכל שכן דניחא השתא הא דלא נקט הכא טעמא דפרישית במתניתין משום דנפקי מתרי קראי:
notes.en: He brings it to sanctity: Rashi explained: that it will rest on Shabbat; and likewise “he abrogates its sanctity”: that the gentile does labor with it on Shabbat. But the expression “sanctity” does not imply this; rather, it means the sanctity of the firstborn, as in the case of Rav Mari bar Raḥel (3b), whose animals all died because he removed them from sanctity, transferring ownership of their ears to a gentile. And although for a purchaser, if the offspring is male, “he brings it to sanctity” does not apply, sometimes the fetus is female, and he brings it to the sanctity of the firstborn, since the offspring of this fetus will be sanctified as a firstborn. And even without the reason “he brings it to sanctity,” the Gemara could have said that there is no reason to penalize him since there is no abrogation, unlike the seller, where there is abrogation; but it preferred to say that there is even a bringing of sanctity. And it could also have given another reason: had the mishna taught only the purchaser, [he is exempt] because he committed no prohibition; but the seller, who committed a prohibition, as it teaches “although he is not permitted,” I would say let us penalize him. The Gemara took one of the two reasons. And all the more so it is well now that it did not give here the reason I explained on the mishna, that they are derived from two verses.

messages.text: But in the case where a Jew sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile, where he abrogates its state of sanctity, I would say that the Sages should penalize him [likneseih] for his actions by rendering the fetus subject to the obligations of firstborn status. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that it is exempt from these obligations.

notes.he: לפדות העובר מן העובד כוכבים וליתנו לכהן:
notes.en: Say: let us penalize him: to redeem the fetus from the gentile and give it to the priest.

notes.he: שאין עושה בו מלאכה בשבת הלכך הקילו על הלוקח עובר שיהא אותו עובר עצמו פטור מן הבכורה. אבל מוכר עובר חמורו דקא מפקע ליה מקדושת שבת ובכורה אימא ליקנסוה שיתן פדיונו לכהן קמ"ל דלא:
notes.en: Because he brings it to sanctity: in that no labor is done with it on Shabbat. Therefore they were lenient with the one who purchases a fetus, that that fetus itself is exempt from the firstborn. But one who sells the fetus of his donkey, as he removes it from the sanctity of Shabbat and of the firstborn, say that they should penalize him, that he give its redemption to the priest. It teaches us that they do not.

messages.text: And why do I need the mishna to state the case of one who enters into a partnership with a gentile?
messages.quote: one who enters into a partnership with a gentile

notes.he: השתא הלוקח היכא דכוליה עובר דישראל פטור משתתף דלית ליה אלא חציו מיבעיא:
notes.en: And why do I need one who enters into a partnership with him? Now, the purchaser, where the entire fetus is the Jew’s, is exempt; the partner, who has only half of it, need it be stated?

messages.text: The case is necessary to exclude the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who says:

notes.he: דאמר לקמן המקבל בהמה מן העובד כוכבים מעלין אותו בשויו ונותן חצי דמיו לכהן:
notes.en: To exclude the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda: who says below: one who receives an animal from a gentile, they assess it at its worth and he gives half its value to the priest.

notes.he: בלא ר' יהודה נמי איצטריך לאשמועינן שותפות דלא שמעינן ליה מרישא אלא כ"ש איצטריך טפי כיון דמשכחת בהא פלוגתא:
notes.en: To exclude the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda: even without Rabbi Yehuda, it would have been necessary to teach us partnership, since we do not learn it from the first clause; but it was all the more necessary, since we find a dispute about this case.

notes.dh: להא אתא לאשמועינן לאפוקי מדרבי יהודה
notes.he: לא אמר בהדיא אלא הכי קאמר לקמן ר' יהודה אומר המקבל בהמה מן העובד כוכבים דהיינו שותפות דמקבלה לפטומה ולחלוק לוולדות:
notes.en: It comes to teach us this, to exclude the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda: he did not say it explicitly, but this is what he says below: Rabbi Yehuda says: one who receives an animal from a gentile; which is a partnership, as he receives it to fatten it and to divide the offspring.

messages.text: An animal owned in partnership with a gentile is obligated, i.e., subject to accounting its offspring a firstborn.
Therefore, the mishna teaches us that it is exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn.

And why do I need the mishna to state that the fetus does not have firstborn status in the case of one who receives a donkey from a gentile in exchange for partnership in its offspring? This halakha is already included in the previous one.
messages.quote: and one who receives a donkey from a gentile

messages.text: It is because the tanna wants to teach in the parallel case of: And one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership, that its offspring does not have firstborn status.
And why do I need the case of one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership to be stated?

It was necessary, because it might enter your mind to say that since the primary animal belongs to the Jew, the Sages should penalize him by treating the offspring as a firstborn and requiring it to be redeemed, lest this case be confused with another case of an animal that the Jew puts in the care of a gentile where the gentile does not own rights to the offspring, and the offspring is counted a firstborn. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that he is not penalized.

notes.he: גוף הבהמה וחצי ולדות:
notes.en: And the primary animal: the body of the animal and half the offspring.

notes.he: שאין לעובד כוכבים חלק בה ולא בוולדותיה ואתי למיפטריה נמי מבכורה:
notes.en: Lest it be confused with another animal: in which the gentile has no share, neither in it nor in its offspring, and one would come to exempt that one too from the firstborn.

notes.he: דאיניש אחרינא דחזי דהאי לא פריק עובר חמורו זה אמר כך לא צריכנא למפרק בכור חמורי דלא ידע דאיהו דלא פרק בכור חמורו משום דיהב ליה בקבלה לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Lest it be confused with another animal: that another person, who sees that this one does not redeem the fetus of his donkey, says: so too I need not redeem the firstborn of my donkey; for he does not know that this one did not redeem the firstborn of his donkey because he gave it to a gentile in receivership.

notes.he: מהו דתימא ליקנסיה דליפרקיה דלא ליתי לאיחלופי קמ"ל דלא:
notes.en: You might say: let us penalize him to redeem it, so that it not come to be confused. It teaches us that we do not.

messages.text: § The Gemara cites a discussion where the mishna is used as a proof: We learned in a mishna elsewhere, with regard to the prohibition against selling large livestock to a gentile due to concern that it will be worked on Shabbat:

notes.he: במסכת ע"ז (דף יד:):
notes.en: We learned there: in tractate Avoda Zara (14b).

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale of a damaged animal permitted because it is incapable of performing labor, and ben Beteira deems the sale of a horse for riding permitted, because riding a horse on Shabbat is not prohibited by Torah law.

notes.he: למכור לעובד כוכבים בהמה שנשברו רגליה ובמקום שלא נחשדו על הרביעה ובן בתירא מתיר בסוס שאין עושין בו מלאכה שיהא בו חיוב חטאת דסתם סוס לרכיבה עומד והרוכב בשבת אינו אלא משום שבות שהחי נושא את עצמו:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda permits a damaged one: to sell to a gentile an animal whose legs are broken, and in a place where they are not suspected of bestiality. And ben Beteira permits a horse, since one does not do with it labor that carries liability for a sin-offering, for an ordinary horse stands for riding, and one who rides on Shabbat [transgresses] only a rabbinic prohibition, since a living being carries itself.

notes.he: הכי רישא דמתניתין אין מוכרין בהמה גסה לעובד כוכבים עגלים וסייחין וקא חשיב כולהו וקתני ר' יהודה מתיר בשבורה למוכרה דלאו בת מלאכה היא ובן בתירא מתיר בסוס שאין עושה בו מלאכה שחייב עליה חטאת דסתם סוס לרכיבה ורכיבה אינה אלא משום שבות דחי נושא את עצמו:
notes.en: We learned there: this is the first clause of that mishna: one does not sell large livestock to gentiles, calves or foals, and it lists all of them, and it teaches: Rabbi Yehuda permits selling a damaged one, since it is not fit for labor; and ben Beteira permits a horse, since one does not do with it labor for which one is liable to a sin-offering, for a horse ordinarily stands for riding, and riding is prohibited only by rabbinic decree, since a living being carries itself.

messages.text: With regard to a fetus, what would Rabbi Yehuda say to me about selling it to a gentile?
messages.lead: A dilemma was raised before the Sages:
messages.quote: Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale of a damaged animal permitted

notes.he: למוכרו לעובד כוכבים שרי או אסור:
notes.en: A fetus, what would Rabbi Yehuda say to me: about selling it to a gentile, is it permitted or prohibited?

notes.he: עובר כשהוא במעי אמו מאי אמר ר' יהודה דמתיר בשבורה מותר האי עובר למוכרו לעובד כוכבים אי לא:
notes.en: A fetus while it is in its mother’s womb, what does Rabbi Yehuda, who permits a damaged one, say? Is it permitted to sell this fetus to a gentile or not?

messages.text: Is the reason that Rabbi Yehuda deems selling the animal permitted there because it is damaged and it cannot work, and a fetus is also damaged in the sense that it cannot work?

notes.he: ואינה ראויה למלאכה:
notes.en: Because it is damaged: and it is not fit for labor.

notes.he: אצל מלאכה:
notes.en: And a fetus too is damaged: with respect to labor.

notes.he: משום דשבורה היא דלא חזי למלאכה:
notes.en: Because it is damaged: and it is not fit for labor.

notes.he: אצל מלאכה:
notes.en: A fetus too is damaged: with respect to labor.

messages.text: Or, perhaps it is permitted to sell a damaged animal because that is not its natural state; it is defective and is therefore not included in the prohibition against selling large livestock. But with regard to a fetus, since that is its natural state, and it will become capable of working after growing up, perhaps it is not considered damaged, as it is not defective.

notes.dh: או דלמא שבורה לאו היינו אורחה
notes.he: דבהמה להיות שבורה הלכך דבר חידוש הוא ולא אתי לאיחלופי ולהתיר מכירת שלמה:
notes.en: Or perhaps damaged, that is not its natural state: for an animal to be damaged; therefore it is something unusual, and people will not come to confuse it and permit selling a whole one.

notes.dh: אבל עובר כיון דהיינו אורחיה לאו שבור הוא
notes.he: פירוש דאתי למיחלף בבהמה אחריתי ועוד מצי למימר משום דעתיד להוליד ולהיות ראוי למלאכה דמהאי טעמא מסקינן דאסור דקאמר והאי עובר נמי כיכול להתרפאות דמי וחד מתרי טעמי נקט:
notes.en: But a fetus, since that is its natural state, is not damaged: meaning that people would come to confuse it with another animal. And the Gemara could also have said: because it will in the future be born and become fit for labor, for by this reason we conclude [below] that it is prohibited, as it says: “and this fetus too is like one that is able to be cured.” It took one of the two reasons.

notes.he: משום הכי מתיר בשבורה דלאו היינו אורחיה שאין דרכה של בהמה שתהא שבורה והשתא כי הויא שבורה שרי לזבונה לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Or perhaps: he permits a damaged one for this reason, that this is not its natural state, as it is not the way of an animal to be damaged; and so when it is damaged it is permitted to sell it to a gentile.

notes.he: אבל עובר היינו אורחיה דהוי כשבור שהוא שבור במעי אמו ועד שהוא קטן לא חזי למלאכה אבל לאו כשבור דמי דהאי אתי לכלל מלאכה לכשיגדיל ולימא דאסר ביה ר' יהודה:
notes.en: But a fetus, that is its natural state: it is like a damaged one, in that it is damaged in its mother’s womb, and while it is small it is not fit for labor; but it is not truly like a damaged one, since it will become fit for labor when it grows up. So let us say that Rabbi Yehuda prohibits it.

messages.text: And one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile, his donkey is exempt from the obligations of firstborn status, although the owner is not permitted to do so. And Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree and claim that he may sell it. Apparently, Rabbi Yehuda agrees that it is prohibited to sell the fetus of one’s animal to a gentile.
messages.lead: Come and hear a resolution to the dilemma from the mishna:
messages.quote: and one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile although he is not permitted

notes.he: דמיירי בעובר וקתני אינו רשאי משום מלאכת שבת:
notes.en: Come and hear: [the mishna,] which deals with a fetus and teaches “he is not permitted,” because of labor on Shabbat.

notes.he: מכלל דסבירא ליה נמי דאינו רשאי למכור עובר לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree in the mishna: by inference, he too holds that one is not permitted to sell a fetus to a gentile.

messages.text: And according to your reasoning, concerning the other cases in the mishna, namely, one who enters into a partnership with a gentile, and one who receives a donkey from a gentile in exchange for partnership in its offspring, and one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership, with regard to which the mishna does not teach that Rabbi Yehuda disagrees, so too does this indicate that he does not disagree with the ruling in the mishna in these cases?

notes.he: דקתני במתני' לענין בכורה דפטור ולא קתני ר' יהודה מחייב ה"נ דלא פליג והא קא חזינן לקמן בשמעתין דפליג בהך ברייתא:
notes.en: And according to your reasoning, one who enters into a partnership with him: which the mishna teaches regarding the firstborn, that it is exempt, and it does not teach “Rabbi Yehuda obligates”; so too [would you say] that he does not disagree? But we see below in this passage that he disagrees in that baraita.

messages.text: That is impossible, as Rabbi Yehuda holds that an animal subject to a partnership between a Jew and gentile is subject to accounting its offspring a firstborn, as is evident from a baraita that will soon be cited.
Rather, clearly Rabbi Yehuda does disagree, but the mishna does not teach his opinion. Here too, with regard to selling the fetus, he disagrees, but the mishna does not teach his opinion.

notes.he: וכי ס"ד דלא פליג בהוו הא איכא דפליג. כדאמרינן לקמן ר' יהודה אומר המקבל בהמה מן העובד כוכבים וילדה מעלין וכו'. שותפין עובדי כוכבים חייב בבכורה אלא פליג אשותפין והוא הדין אכולהו ואי לא קתני פלוגתא במתניתין פליג בברייתא ומדפליג ש"מ לר' יהודה מותר למכור עובר לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: That it does not teach that Rabbi Yehuda disagrees: and would it enter your mind that he does not disagree about them? But there is a place where he disagrees, as we say below: Rabbi Yehuda says: one who receives an animal from a gentile and it gave birth, they assess it, etc.; [so for him an animal of] partners with a gentile is obligated in the firstborn. Rather, he disagrees about partners, and the same is true of all of them; and if the mishna does not teach the dispute, he disagrees in a baraita. And since he disagrees, learn from it that according to Rabbi Yehuda it is permitted to sell a fetus to a gentile.

messages.text: Come and hear a resolution from a baraita:

In the case of one who receives an animal from a gentile in order to care for it and receives some of the offspring in exchange for his work, and it gave birth to a firstborn, they assess its value, and the Jew gives half of its value to the priest to redeem his portion, which is sanctified by the firstborn status.

notes.dh: רבי יהודה אומר המקבל בהמה כו' וילדה
notes.he: בכור:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: one who receives an animal, etc., and it gave birth: to a firstborn.

notes.he: שמין:
notes.en: They assess [ma’alin]: they appraise.

notes.he: אבל קדושת הגוף לא קדוש ליקרב למזבח הואיל וחציו לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: And he gives half its value to the priest: but it is not sanctified with inherent sanctity, to be offered on the altar, since half of it belongs to the gentile.

notes.he: לא לקדש קדושת הגוף להיות קרב למזבח מפני חלקו של עובד כוכבים כדפי' בקונט' ובסוף פרקא שרי ליה ר' יהודה בגיזה ובעבודה דדריש ליה לא תעבוד בבכור שורך אבל אתה עובד בשלך ובשל אחרים ולא תגוז בכור צאנך אבל אתה גוזז בשלך ובשל אחרים וא"ת נהי דלא קדוש קדושת הגוף מ"מ כיון דמדאורייתא חייבת בבכורה אותו חלק שיש לו בו יהא של כהן למה נותן לכהן דמי חלקו י"ל משום טיבותא דכהן לא ניחא ליה בשותפות עובד כוכבים לפי שאינו יכול להוציא חלקו מיד עובד כוכבים במהרה כל כך וא"ת ובסיפא דקתני קונסין אותו עד עשרה בדמיו אי איירי בפטר חמור ניחא טפי ברישא ובסיפא שנותן דמיה לפי שאין הפטר חמור עצמו ניתן לכהן אלא נפדה בשה כל דהו או בשויו כדאמר לקמן (בכורות דף ט.):
notes.en: And he gives half its value to the priest: it is not sanctified with inherent sanctity, to be offered on the altar, because of the gentile’s share, as Rashi explained. And at the end of the chapter (3b) Rabbi Yehuda permits it in shearing and in labor, as he expounds: “You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox” (Deuteronomy 15:19), but you may work with one that is yours and others’; “nor shear the firstborn of your flock,” but you may shear one that is yours and others’. And if you will say: granted that it is not sanctified with inherent sanctity, nevertheless, since by Torah law it is obligated in the firstborn, the share he has in it should belong to the priest; why does he give the priest the value of his share? One can say: for the priest’s benefit, since a partnership with a gentile does not suit him, as he cannot remove his share from the gentile’s hand so quickly. And as for the latter clause, which teaches “they penalize him up to ten times its value”: if it deals with a firstborn donkey, it is easier to understand, in both the first and the latter clause, that he gives its value, since the firstborn donkey itself is not given to the priest but is redeemed with any lamb or with its value, as stated below (Bekhorot 9a).

notes.he: דשמין אותו וולד (בשווה) כמה הוא שווה ונותן חצי דמיו לכהן החצי שהוא שלו:
notes.en: They assess it at its worth: they appraise that offspring, how much it is worth, and he gives half its value to the priest, the half that is his.

messages.text: And in the case of one who gives the gentile an animal in receivership even though he is not permitted to do so, the Sages penalize him by requiring that he purchase the gentile’s portion of the animal for up to ten times its value, and he gives all of its value to the priest.

notes.he: נמי לא קדוש קדושת הגוף הואיל וחציו לעובד כוכבים פטור מן הבכורה והא דיהיב כל דמיו לכהן קנסא הוא שקונסין אותו לפי שמכרה לעובד כוכבים והנותן לו בקבלה אף על פי שאינו רשאי כלומר שאף על פי שאינו רשאי (לתנו לו) לעובד כוכבים במתנה:
notes.en: And one who gives it to him in receivership: this too is not sanctified with inherent sanctity, since half of it is the gentile’s; it is exempt from the firstborn. And that he gives all its value to the priest is a penalty, as they penalize him because he sold it to a gentile. And “one who gives it to him in receivership although he is not permitted”: that is to say, although he is not permitted to give it to a gentile even as a gift.

notes.he: הואיל ולא חש לדברי חכמים:
notes.en: They penalize him: since he paid no heed to the words of the Sages.

notes.he: דוקא בגסה קנסו אבל דקה כיון דאיסורא ליכא אלא מנהגא בעלמא במקום שחשודים על הרביעה דעובד כוכבים חס על בהמתו שלא תעקר לא קנסו אפילו במקום שלא נהגו למכור ולקמן אמר ריש לקיש מוכר בהמה גסה לעובד כוכבים קונסין אותו עד עשרה בדמיו דוקא גסה אבל דקה לא:
notes.en: They penalize him up to ten times its value: they penalized specifically for large livestock. But for small livestock, since there is no prohibition but merely a custom, in a place where they are suspected of bestiality, as a gentile has compassion on his own animal that it not become barren, they did not penalize, even in a place where they were not accustomed to sell. And below (3a) Reish Lakish says: one who sells large livestock to a gentile, they penalize him up to ten times its value: specifically large livestock, but not small.

notes.he: אע"פ שאינו רשאי ליתנו לעובד כוכבים בקבלה לפי שעושה בה מלאכה בשבת ועוד שמפקיעו מן הבכורה:
notes.en: Although he is not permitted to give it to a gentile in receivership: because the gentile does labor with it on Shabbat, and furthermore because he removes it from the firstborn.

notes.he: שיפדה העובר מן העובד כוכבים אפי' שאינו יכול לפדותו מן העובד כוכבים אם לא יתן לו עשר ידות יותר מכדי דמיו:
notes.en: They penalize him up to ten, etc.: that he must redeem the fetus from the gentile, even if he cannot redeem it from the gentile unless he gives him ten parts beyond its value.

notes.he: ונותן דמיו של עובר לכהן ואע"ג דכתיב תפדה בשה יכול לפדותו אפי' בדמים כדאמרינן באידך פירקא דלא באתה תורה להחמיר עליו אלא להקל עליו אבל שאר בכורות בהמה טהורה אין פודין אותן בדמים אלא נותן הבכור לכהן ואם רצה הכהן למוכרו לו רשאי ומ"ט נותן כל דמיו לכהן ולא סגי בחצי דמיו משום דעיקר בהמה דישראל:
notes.en: And he gives the value of the fetus to the priest: and although it is written “you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 13:13), he may redeem it even with money, as we say in the other chapter, for the Torah came not to be stringent with him but to be lenient with him. But other firstborns, of a kosher animal, are not redeemed with money; rather, he gives the firstborn to the priest, and if the priest wishes to sell it to him, he may. And what is the reason he gives all its value to the priest, and half its value does not suffice? Because the primary animal is the Jew’s.

messages.text: 2b
What, is it not referring to the fetus when the baraita states that he is not permitted to sell it?
messages.quote: even though he is not permitted

notes.he: קאמר דאינו רשאי:
notes.en: What, is it not referring to the fetus: when it says “he is not permitted”?

notes.he: הא דקתני קונסין לאו אעובר קאי ומשום דאינו רשאי אלמא דר' יהודה סבר דאסור למכור עובר לעובד כוכבים הואיל דהיינו אורחיה:
notes.en: What, is it not: that which it teaches “they penalize,” does it not refer to the fetus, and because “he is not permitted”? Evidently Rabbi Yehuda holds that it is prohibited to sell a fetus to a gentile, since that is its natural state.

messages.text: No, it is referring to the animal itself that he may not sell to the gentile, and that is why he is penalized.

notes.he: פי' ואיירי בבהמה מעוברת. לא אבהמה פי' ולא איירי בעובר אלא בבהמה לעוברה וכן משמע לקמן גבי בעיא דבהמה לעובריה מהו ובעי למיפשט מהכא דאסור דקאמר מאי לאו אבהמה ש"מ דאי אבהמה קאי איירי בבהמה לעוברה ולכאורה לא איירי בבהמה לעוברה דא"כ מאי פריך והא דמיו קתני לימא דקאי אעובר וכי תימא דמשמע ליה דקאי אבהמה א"כ לקמן נמי לידוק הכי אלא הכא איירי בבהמה לפטומה כדמסיק לקמן לעוברה:
notes.en: What, is it not referring to the fetus: meaning, and it deals with a pregnant animal. No, to the animal: meaning, and it does not deal with a fetus but with an animal sold for its fetus. And so it is implied below, regarding the dilemma “an animal sold for its fetuses, what is the halakha?”, where the Gemara seeks to resolve from here that it is prohibited, saying “What, is it not referring to the animal?” Learn from it that if it refers to the animal, it deals with an animal sold for its fetus. But seemingly it does not deal with an animal sold for its fetus, for if so, what is the challenge “but it teaches its value [damav]”? Let us say it refers to the fetus [to come]. And if you say that it seemed to the Gemara to refer to the animal, then below too let it infer so. Rather, here it deals with an animal given for fattening, as the Gemara concludes, [and below] with an animal sold for its fetus.

notes.he: דקונסין אותו אבל עובר רשאי למכור:
notes.en: It refers to the animal: that they penalize him for it; but a fetus he is permitted to sell.

messages.text: But doesn’t the baraita teach: The Sages penalize him up to ten times its value [damav], in masculine form, indicating that it is referring to the fetus and not the mother?
messages.quote: up to ten times its value

notes.he: דמשמע דמי עובר:
notes.en: But it teaches “up to ten times its value [damav]”: which implies the value of the fetus.

messages.text: Teach the following wording in the baraita: The Sages penalize him up to ten times its value [dameha], in feminine form.

notes.he: דמשמע של בהמה:
notes.en: Teach “its value [dameha]”: which implies the value of the animal.

notes.he: ואי בהמה קא בעית למימר כל דמיה:
notes.en: And if you wish to say it refers to the animal, [read] “all its [the animal’s] value.”

messages.text: But doesn’t it teach: He gives all of its value to the priest? And if it is referring to the animal and not the firstborn, what is the relevance of the priest?

notes.he: בבהמה אלא ודאי אעובר:
notes.en: What is the relevance of the priest: to the animal? Rather, certainly it refers to the fetus.

notes.dh: כהן מאי עבידתיה בבהמה עצמה אמאי יהיב ליה כל דמיה
notes.he: אלא לאו אעובר קאי:
notes.en: What is the relevance of the priest to the animal itself? Why does he give him all its value? Rather, is it not referring to the fetus?

messages.text: Here we are dealing with a case where the Jew gave the gentile a pregnant animal to fatten it in order to divide the profits as well as the offspring. Since we penalize him for selling the animal in a prohibited manner, we penalize him with regard to the fetus as well.

notes.he: לעולם מהכא לא תפשוט דהכא במאי עסקינן כגון דיהיב ליה בהמה מעברתא לפטומה וליטול חצי השבח בין בפטום בין בוולדות דמיגו דקנסינן וכו' אבל אי זבין ליה עובר לחודיה לא:
notes.en: No: actually, do not resolve the question from here, for here, with what are we dealing? For example, where he gave him a pregnant animal to fatten and to take half the improvement, both in the fattening and in the offspring; since we penalize him, etc. But if he sold him the fetus alone, no.

notes.he: לא לעולם סבירא ליה בעלמא דמוכרין עובר לעובד כוכבים דכשבור הוא והכא מאי שנא דקתני קונסין דמשמע נמי אעובר כגון דיהב ליה לעובד כוכבים בהמה מעוברת לפטומה דלכי מיפטמה לה ליזבנו וליחלקו דמיה דהשתא אבהמה גופה קנסי ליה ומיגו דקנסי ליה כו'. והיינו ונותן כל דמיו לכהן אבל בעלמא שרי לזבוני לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: No: actually he holds in general that one may sell a fetus to a gentile, as it is like a damaged one. And here, what is different, that it teaches “they penalize,” which implies the fetus as well? For example, where he gave a gentile a pregnant animal to fatten, so that when it is fattened they will sell it and divide its value; now they penalize him for the animal itself, and since they penalize him, etc. And this is “and he gives all its value to the priest.” But in general it is permitted to sell [a fetus] to a gentile.

messages.text: Come and hear a resolution from a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale to a gentile of a damaged animal permitted, because it is incapable of being cured.

notes.he: ולעשות מלאכה בשבת:
notes.en: That cannot be cured: and do labor on Shabbat.

messages.text: This statement indicates that if it is capable of being cured, Rabbi Yehuda deems its sale prohibited. And a fetus is also similar to one who is able to be cured, as it ultimately will be capable of working. Learn from it that Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale of a fetus to a gentile prohibited.

notes.he: והאי נמי כיכול להתרפאות דמי דלכשיגדיל חזי למלאכה ש"מ דעובר אסור למכור לעובד כוכבים לר' יהודה:
notes.en: And this too is like one that is able to be cured, for when it grows up it is fit for labor. Learn from it that according to Rabbi Yehuda it is prohibited to sell a fetus to a gentile.

messages.text: And there are those who teach this discussion as referring to the statement in the mishna:
With regard to one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile, although he is not permitted to sell a large animal to a gentile, it is exempt from the obligations of firstborn status.
messages.quote: and one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile although he is not permitted

notes.he: הא דר' יהודה אמתניתין ולא בעי לה מיבעיא:
notes.en: There are those who teach it: this statement of Rabbi Yehuda, as referring to the mishna, and they do not raise it as a dilemma.

messages.text: Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as we learned in a mishna:

notes.he: לימא מתני' דלא כר' יהודה דמדשרי ר' יהודה בשבורה ה"ה דשרי נמי אעובר וכשבור דמי:
notes.en: Let us say the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: for since Rabbi Yehuda permits a damaged one, the same is true that he permits a fetus too, as it is like a damaged one.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale of a damaged animal permitted because it is incapable of performing labor.

notes.he: ועובר דומיא דשבורה:
notes.en: Permits a damaged one: and a fetus is similar to a damaged one.

messages.text: The halakha is presumably the same with regard to a fetus, which is also not capable of performing labor.

You may even say that it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is permitted to sell a damaged animal because that is not its natural state; it is defective and is therefore not included in the prohibition against selling large livestock. But with regard to a fetus, since it is in its natural state, and will become capable of working after growing up, perhaps it is not considered damaged, as it is not defective.

notes.he: ולא שבור הוי:
notes.en: That is its natural state: and it is not damaged.

notes.he: ובשבורה (שרי אסר) [הוא דשרי] דלאו היינו אורחיה כדאמר לעיל אבל בעובר אסר דהיינו אורחיה למיהוי כשבור עד שהוא במעי אמו אבל לבסוף חזי למלאכה ואסור:
notes.en: You may even say it is Rabbi Yehuda: and it is a damaged one that he permits, since that is not its natural state, as he said above; but a fetus he prohibits, since it is its natural state to be like a damaged one while it is in its mother’s womb, but in the end it is fit for labor; so it is prohibited.

messages.text: Come and hear another proof from a baraita:

In the case of one who receives an animal from a gentile to care for and receives a portion of the offspring in exchange for his work, and it gave birth to a firstborn, they assess its value, and the Jew gives half of its value to the priest to redeem his portion, which is sanctified by the firstborn status. And in the case of one who gives the gentile an animal in receivership even though he is not permitted to do so, the Sages penalize him by requiring that he purchase the gentile’s portion of the animal for up to ten times its value, and he gives all of its value to the priest.
What, is it not referring to the fetus when the baraita states that he is not permitted to sell it?
messages.quote: even though he is not permitted

messages.text: No, it is referring to the animal itself that he may not sell to the gentile, and that is why he is penalized.
But doesn’t the baraita teach: The Sages penalize him up to ten times its value [damav], in masculine form, indicating that it is referring to the fetus and not the mother?
Teach the following wording in the baraita: The Sages penalize him up to ten times its value [dameha], in feminine form.
But doesn’t it teach: He gives all of its value to the priest? And if it is referring to the animal and not the firstborn, what is the relevance of the priest?

Here we are dealing with a case where the Jew gave the gentile a pregnant animal to fatten it in order to divide the profits as well as the offspring. Since we penalize him for selling the animal in a prohibited manner, we penalize him with regard to the fetus as well.
Come and hear a resolution from a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale to a gentile of a damaged animal permitted, because it is incapable of being cured.

This statement indicates that if it is capable of being cured, Rabbi Yehuda deems its sale prohibited. And this fetus is also similar to one who is able to be cured, as it ultimately will be capable of working. Learn from it that Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale of a fetus to a gentile prohibited.

In the case of a Jew who sold an animal to a gentile only with regard to rights to its fetuses, but retained ownership of the animal itself, what is the halakha concerning the permissibility of the sale?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages concerning the prohibition against selling large livestock to a gentile:

notes.he: כגון שעדיין לא נתעברה ומכר לו כל הוולדות שעתידין להתעבר ובהמה עצמה לא מכר לו:
notes.en: An animal for its fetuses: for example, where it is not yet pregnant, and he sold him all the offspring that it will conceive in the future, but the animal itself he did not sell him.

notes.he: לקונסו לפדותה משום מוכר בהמה לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: What is the halakha: is he penalized and made to redeem it, because of [the prohibition on] one who sells an animal to a gentile?

notes.he: שאינה מעוברת לעובד כוכבים לעובריה שיהיו העוברין של שניהם:
notes.en: He sold an animal: that is not pregnant, to a gentile, for its fetuses, so that the fetuses will belong to both of them.

messages.text: Let the dilemma be raised according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who permits the sale of a damaged animal, and let the dilemma be raised according to the opinion of the Rabbis, who dispute that ruling.

notes.he: תיבעי לתרוייהו דהכא לא מזבין לא בהמה עצמה ולא עובר דאכתי לא מיעברא:
notes.en: Let it be raised according to both of them: for here he sells neither the animal itself nor a fetus, since it is not yet pregnant.

messages.text: Let the dilemma be raised according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as follows: Perhaps Rabbi Yehuda permits only the sale of a damaged animal, as people will not come to confuse this animal with a healthy animal, which is prohibited for sale to a gentile, as they are visibly different. But in the case of one who sells an unblemished animal with regard to the rights to its fetuses, which people may come to confuse with the case of selling the animal entirely and consider that sale permitted as well, Rabbi Yehuda deems the sale prohibited.

notes.he: להתיר מכירת שלמה:
notes.en: That people will come to confuse: and permit selling a whole one.

notes.he: בשבורה דלא אתיא לאיחלופי בשלמה:
notes.en: A damaged one, which will not be confused with a whole one.

notes.he: היכא דזבין בהמה לעובריה דבהמה גופה שלמה היא ואתי לאיחלופי במכירה שלמה אחריתי שלא לעובריה לחלוטין ואסר:
notes.en: But a whole one: where he sold an animal for its fetuses, and the animal itself is whole, it will come to be confused with another sale of a whole animal, sold outright and not for its fetuses; so he prohibits it.

messages.text: Or perhaps Rabbi Yehuda would claim that in the case of a damaged animal, which is separated from him in its entirety in the sale, the sale is permitted, and all the more so with regard to the sale of an unblemished animal with regard to the rights to its fetuses, where the animal is not entirely separated from him, as he did not sell the actual animal, the sale is permitted.

notes.he: שלא שייר בה לעצמו כלום משמכרה:
notes.en: Which is separated from him: as he retained nothing in it for himself once he sold it.

notes.he: כי האי גוונא דלא פסקה מיניה שהרי שייר לעצמו גוף הבהמה ואי משום עוברין ליכא למיחש שהרי לא נתעברה עדיין ולא כלום מכר לו ולכשיבאו ברשות עובד כוכבים הם באים:
notes.en: And all the more so an unblemished one: in such a case, which is not separated from him, since he retained the body of the animal for himself; and as for the fetuses, there is no concern, since it has not yet conceived and he sold him nothing, and when they come, they come into being in the gentile’s domain.

notes.dh: או דלמא ומה שבורה דפסקה מיניה
notes.he: דלחלוטין מזבנה לעובד כוכבים דאע"ג דאיכא למיחש אטו מכירה חלוטה אחר דשלמה אפי' הכי שרי:
notes.en: Or perhaps: if a damaged one, which is separated from him, as he sells it outright to the gentile, although there is concern for confusion with another outright sale of a whole one, is even so permitted,

messages.text: Likewise, the dilemma can be raised according to the opinion of the Rabbis: Perhaps the Rabbis deemed the sale prohibited only in a case of a damaged animal, as the animal is separated from him. But in the case of an unblemished animal that is sold only with regard to the fetuses, where it is not separated from him, and there is no concern that people will mistakenly sell the entire animal to a gentile, they deem the sale permitted.

notes.he: ומכירה חלוטה היא ואתי לאחלופי ולהתיר מכירה חלוטה שלמה אבל הכא דלא פסקה מיניה שרי דלאו מכירה היא:
notes.en: As it is separated from him: and it is an outright sale, and people will come to confuse it and permit an outright sale of a whole one. But here, where it is not separated from him, it is permitted, as it is not a sale.

messages.text: Or perhaps the Rabbis would claim that in the case of a damaged animal, which people will not come to confuse with the case of an unblemished animal, the Rabbis deem the sale prohibited, and all the more so they would prohibit selling an unblemished animal with regard to the rights to its fetuses, which people may come to confuse with the case of selling an unblemished animal in its entirety.

notes.he: במכירה חלוטה של שלימה אחרת:
notes.en: And all the more so an unblemished one, which people may come to confuse: with an outright sale of another whole one.

notes.he: וכ"ש שלימה לעובריה דלא פסקה מיניה דלא מזבנה לגמרי דשרי או דלמא לרבנן ומה שבורה דלא אתי לחלופי בשלימה אפי' הכי אסרי רבנן דלמא אתי לחלופי מכירה חלוטה דשלמה אטו מכירה חלוטה דהא וכ"ש שלמה לעובריה דאתי לחלופי שלמה בשלמה ומיחש לחלוטין וקא ס"ד מאן דאסר (שלימה) [בהמה] לעובר' דלמא אתי לאיחלופי בבהמה אחריתי לחלוטין וה"ה דאוסר נמי למוכרה לעובד כוכבים לגיזה ולחלבה דאיכא למימר נמי דלמא אתי לאיחלופי הא מכירה דשלימה אטו שלימה אחריתי דחלוטין:
notes.en: then all the more so a whole one sold for its fetuses, which is not separated from him, as he does not sell it entirely, is permitted. Or perhaps, according to the Rabbis: if a damaged one, which will not be confused with a whole one, the Rabbis even so prohibit, lest one come to confuse an outright sale of a whole one with the outright sale of this one, then all the more so a whole one sold for its fetuses, which will come to be confused, a whole one with a whole one, and one should be concerned for an outright sale. And it entered the Gemara’s mind that whoever prohibits an animal sold for its fetuses, lest it be confused with another animal sold outright, likewise also prohibits selling it to a gentile for its shearing and its milk, since there too one can say: lest one come to confuse this sale of a whole one with another whole one sold outright.

messages.caption: The dilemma: each side’s ruling on a damaged animal can be read two ways, and each reading points to a different answer for selling only the future fetuses.

messages.text: And is the reason of the opinion of the Rabbis due to that concern that people may confuse the sale of a damaged animal with the sale of an unblemished animal in its entirety? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

notes.he: בתמיה דאיצטריך לן למיבעי:
notes.en: Is it for this reason: said in astonishment, that we needed to raise the dilemma.

notes.he: ומי מצית אמרת דהאי דקא אסרי רבנן בשלימה משום דאתיא לאיחלופי ומי תלי טעמא באיחלופי:
notes.en: And is the reason of the Rabbis because of this? Can you say that the Rabbis prohibit a whole one because it will come to be confused? Does their reason depend on confusion?

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehuda But why do you hold that it is permitted to sell a damaged animal? Don’t they breed it with another animal, and it gives birth to offspring, which will then be owned by a gentile?

notes.he: על השבורה:
notes.en: With it: with the damaged one.

messages.text: Apparently, the reason the Rabbis prohibit the sale is due to the animal’s fetuses. If so, they should prohibit selling large livestock to a gentile with regard to the fetuses as well.

notes.he:
טעמא דרבנן משום עוברין תיפשוט מינה דלרבנן אסור למכור לעובד כוכבים בהמה לעובריה ולר' יהודה מותר:
לעולם טעמא דרבנן משום איחלופי ואיצטריך למיבעי כיון דלא פסקה מיניה איכא למימר לא אתי לאיחלופי במכירה גמורה והכי קאמרי ליה רבנן לר' יהודה:
notes.en: Apparently: the reason of the Rabbis is because of the fetuses. Resolve from it that according to the Rabbis it is prohibited to sell an animal to a gentile for its fetuses, and according to Rabbi Yehuda it is permitted. [The answer:] Actually, the reason of the Rabbis is because of confusion, and it was necessary to raise the dilemma, since, as it is not separated from him, one can say that people will not come to confuse it with a complete sale. And this is what the Rabbis are saying to Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: This is not truly the Rabbis’ opinion. Rather, this is what they were saying to Rabbi Yehuda:
messages.quote: Don’t they breed it with another animal, and it gives birth

notes.dh: אמרו לו לר' יהודה אמאי קא שרית בשבורה והלא מרביעין עליה ויולדת
notes.he: ונמצא דבהמה (גופה) [גסה] שלמה מכר לו אלמא דטעמייהו דרבנן דאסרי משום עובר הוא משום דאסור למכור עובר לעובד כוכבים ולא משום איחלופי וכיון דלא חיישינן לאיחלופי אלא משום עובר ש"מ לגיזה ולחלבה שרי בשבורה ולעולם טעמא דרבנן דחיישי לאיחלופי והם הכי אסרי לגיזה ולחלבה והכי קאמרי ליה וכו' מ"ט קא שרית בשבורה כמאן דזבנה ניהליה לשחיטה דמי דמיד נוחרה וליכא דידע דזבנה לעובד כוכבים ולא אתי לחלופי מכירה חלוטה למכירה חלוטה דהא מיד נוחרה וליתה בעין ודאי ליכא למימר הכי דמיד נוחרה. (אבל אם) [דהלא] משהי לה כדי להרביעה שתלד וכיון דמשהי לה אתי לחלופי אטו מכירה חלוטה ואמאי קא שרית הא אינו נוחרה:
notes.en: They said to Rabbi Yehuda: why do you permit a damaged one? But don’t they breed it and it gives birth, and it turns out that he sold him a whole large animal? Evidently the reason of the Rabbis who prohibit is because of the fetus, since it is prohibited to sell a fetus to a gentile, and not because of confusion; and since we are concerned not about confusion but only about the fetus, learn from it that a damaged one sold for its shearing and its milk is permitted. But actually the reason of the Rabbis is that they are concerned about confusion, and for that reason they prohibit selling for shearing and milk, and this is what they are saying to him, etc.: What is the reason you permit a damaged one? It is like one who sold it to him for slaughter, since he will kill it immediately, and no one will know that he sold it to a gentile, and one will not come to confuse an outright sale with an outright sale, since he kills it immediately and it is no longer extant. But certainly one cannot say that he kills it immediately, for doesn’t he keep it in order to breed it, so that it gives birth? And since he keeps it, one will come to confuse it with an outright sale. So why do you permit it, since he does not kill it?

messages.alt: as the Gemara explains their words
messages.text: @Rabbi Yehuda Our reason for prohibiting the sale of a damaged animal is because people might come to confuse this case with the sale of an unblemished animal. But you, what is the reason that you permit selling a damaged animal? It is because the animal is incapable of being cured, and you therefore consider it similar to one who sold an animal explicitly for slaughter, which is permitted.

notes.he: וליכא למיחש לאיחלופי דמאן דחזי ידע דלא מזבין ליה אלא לשחיטה ולא אתי לזבוני בהמה שלא לשחיטה:
notes.en: It is like one who sold it for slaughter: and there is no concern about confusion, since whoever sees it knows that he sold it to him only for slaughter, and will not come to sell an animal not for slaughter.

messages.alt: as the Gemara explains their words
messages.text: But actually it is not similar to that case, as don’t they breed a damaged animal with another animal, and it gives birth? And since they breed it and it gives birth, the gentile will delay its slaughter. Others may then mistakenly believe that selling large livestock for purposes other than slaughter is permitted.

notes.he: לצורך וולדות ומאן דחזי לה בבית העובד כוכבים לסוף שנה או שתים סבר מותר למכור בהמה לעובד כוכבים שלא לשחיטה:
notes.en: He delays it: for the sake of the offspring, and one who sees it in the gentile’s house at the end of a year or two thinks it is permitted to sell an animal to a gentile not for slaughter.

messages.text: @The Sages When a damaged animal actually gives birth, I will concern myself with this possibility.

notes.he: כלומר כשתראו שום שבורה בעולם שיולדת תימרו לי מ"ט שרית בשבורה דודאי אינה יולדת:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda said to them: when it gives birth. That is to say, when you see any damaged animal in the world that gives birth, then ask me why I permit a damaged one; for certainly it does not give birth.

messages.text: Practically, this concern may be disregarded, as such an animal cannot breed with a male. In any event, no proof may be brought from this baraita concerning the opinion of the Rabbis concerning selling an animal with regard to the rights to its fetuses.

notes.he: לא מטעם טרפות מדאמר פרק אלו טריפות (חולין דף נז:) גבי ר"ש [בן חלפתא] שהיה עסקן בדברים ודילמא קסבר ר' יהודה טריפה יולדת ומשבחת ואית ספרים דלא גרסי יולדת שאין צורך שם בלידה אלא במה שמשבחת ומ"מ מסתבר הכא דאפילו מן הארכובה ולמטה שרי רבי יהודה משום דלא מקבלה זכר:
notes.en: For it does not accept a male: not because of being a tereifa [which cannot give birth], since it is said in Chullin 57b (Elu Tereifot), regarding Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta, who was an investigator of things: “And perhaps Rabbi Yehuda holds that a tereifa gives birth and thrives.” Some books do not read “gives birth” there, as there is no need there for giving birth, only for thriving. In any case, it is reasonable here that Rabbi Yehuda permits even [an animal broken] from the knee down, because it does not accept a male.

notes.he: משום דשבורה היא ואינה יכולה לסובלו הלכך שרי ר' יהודה דלא חייש דלמא משהי לה לצורך וולדות. אבל שלמה לעובריה לר' יהודה עדיין תיבעי לך:
notes.en: For it does not accept a male: because it is damaged and cannot bear him. Therefore Rabbi Yehuda permits it, as he is not concerned that the gentile might keep it for the sake of offspring. But a whole one sold for its fetuses, according to Rabbi Yehuda, is still a dilemma for you.

messages.text: And in the case of one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership, meaning that he divides the offspring with him in exchange for caring for the animal, the donkey is exempt from the obligations of firstborn status. This case is identical to that of selling an animal with regard to the rights to its fetuses, and the mishna does not teach: Although he is not permitted to do so. Apparently such a sale is permitted.
messages.lead: Come and hear a proof from the mishna, where it states:
messages.quote: and one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership

notes.he: ממתני':
notes.en: Come and hear: from the mishna.

notes.he: אלמא מותר למכור בהמה לעובריה דהא קבלה מכירה לעוברין היא שאין חולק העובד כוכבים אלא בוולדות דקס"ד דלא פליג עובד כוכבים בשבח פטימת בהמה:
notes.en: And it does not teach “although he is not permitted”: evidently it is permitted to sell an animal for its fetuses, since receivership is a sale for the fetuses, as the gentile shares only in the offspring; for the Gemara assumed that the gentile does not share in the improvement from fattening the animal.

notes.he: ולא קתני אנותן לו בקבלה אע"פ שאינו רשאי מדלא תני הכי ש"מ דסבירא להו לרבנן דמוכר בהמה לעובר דקבלה היינו למחצית שבח וולדות והיינו בבהמה לעובריה:
notes.en: And it does not teach regarding one who gives it to him in receivership “although he is not permitted”: since it does not teach this, learn from it that the Rabbis hold that one who sells an animal for its fetus [is permitted], for receivership is for half the improvement and the offspring, and this is an animal sold for its fetuses.

messages.text: But according to your reasoning, with regard to that which the mishna states: One who enters into a partnership with a gentile, where it also does not teach: Although he is not permitted to do so, so too, should it be derived that it is permitted to enter into such a partnership? But doesn’t Shmuel’s father say:

notes.he: מקבלה לא שייך להקשות דמיתסר משום שותפין דלא אתי בקבלה כל כך לידי שבועה ודוקא נקט שותפות אבל שאר משא ומתן לא אסור:
notes.en: And according to your reasoning, one who enters into a partnership with him, etc.: regarding receivership it is not apt to challenge that it should be prohibited because of partnership, since receivership does not lead to an oath so much. And the Gemara specifically took partnership; but other commerce is not prohibited.

notes.he: דלא קתני אע"פ שאינו רשאי הכי נמי דרשאי להשתתף:
notes.en: And according to your reasoning, one who enters into a partnership: where it does not teach “although he is not permitted,” so too is he permitted to enter a partnership?

messages.text: It is prohibited for a person to enter into a partnership with a gentile lest their joint ventures lead them to quarrel and his gentile partner will be obligated to take an oath to him and he will take an oath in the name of his object of idol worship; and the Torah states: “Neither let it be heard out of your mouth,” which includes causing a gentile to take an oath in the name of an idol.

verse.he: וּבְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־אָמַרְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶם תִּשָּׁמֵרוּ וְשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים לֹא תַזְכִּירוּ לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל־פִּיךָ׃
verse.en: Be on guard concerning all that I have told you. Make no mention of the names of other gods; they shall not be heard on your lips.

notes.he: בהגרמת פיך:
notes.en: Out of your mouth: by your mouth’s causing it.

notes.dh: אסור לאדם שיעשה שותפות עם העובד כוכבים
notes.he: הא דתניא פ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף כב.) ישראל ועובד כוכבים שקבלו שדה בשותפות וכן עובדא דעובד כוכבים נוטל שני ערלה וישראל נוטל שני היתר ואמר פרק הזרוע (חולין דף קלג.) המשתתף עם עובד כוכבים צריך שירשום כל הני עובדא פליגי אאבוה דשמואל:
notes.en: It is prohibited for a person to enter into a partnership with a gentile: what is taught in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (22a), a Jew and a gentile who received a field in partnership; and likewise the case where the gentile takes the years of orla and the Jew takes the permitted years; and what is said in Chullin 133a (HaZero’a), one who enters into a partnership with a gentile must mark [his share]: all these disagree with Shmuel’s father.

notes.dh: שמא יתחייב לו עובד כוכבים שבועה
notes.he: מכאן אוסר רבינו שמואל קבלת השבועה מק"ו ור"ת מתיר מפני שהוא כמציל מידם כדתניא פ"ק דמס' ע"ז (דף ו:) מלוה על פה גובין מהן מפני שהוא כמציל מידם אע"ג דאזיל ומודה ויש לחלק בין ספק לודאי עוד מייתי ר"ת ראיה מההיא דפרק [בתרא] דמגילה (דף כח.) דאמר אבוה בר איהי תיתי לי דלא עבדי שותפות עם עובד כוכבים ואי אסור מאי רבותיה וכן פר"ת שלא היו נזהרים משלש סעודות מדאמר פרק כל כתבי (שבת דף קיח:) תיתי לי דקיימית ג' סעודות משמע שכולן לא היו נזהרים בהן עוד פר"ת בזמן הזה כולן נשבעים בקדשים ואין תופסין בהם אלהות ואע"פ שמזכירין [עמהם] שם שמים וכוונתם [לד"א מ"מ] אין זה [שם] עבודת כוכבים כי דעתם לשם עושה שמים וארץ ואע"ג שמשתתף ש"ש ודבר אחר אין כאן לפני עור לא תתן מכשול דבני נח לא הוזהרו על כך ולדידן לא אשכחן איסור בגרם שיתוף:
notes.en: Lest the gentile become obligated to take an oath to him: from here Rabbeinu Shmuel prohibits accepting an oath [from a gentile], by an a fortiori inference. Rabbeinu Tam permits it, since it is like rescuing [one’s money] from them, as is taught in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (6b): a loan by word of mouth may be collected from them [on their festival], because it is like rescuing it from them, even though he goes and gives thanks [to his idol]. One can distinguish, though, between a possibility and a certainty. Rabbeinu Tam further brings proof from the last chapter of Megilla (28a), where Avuh bar Ihi said: “May [a reward] come to me, for I never made a partnership with a gentile”: if it were prohibited, what was his special merit? And likewise Rabbeinu Tam explained that people were not careful about the three Shabbat meals, since it says in Shabbat 118b: “May [a reward] come to me, for I kept three meals,” implying that not everyone was careful about them. Rabbeinu Tam further explained that nowadays they all swear by their holy objects and do not treat them as divinity; and although they mention the name of Heaven with them and intend something else, nevertheless this is not the name of idolatry, as their intention is to the Maker of heaven and earth. And although they associate the name of Heaven with something else, there is no [violation of] “Before the blind do not place a stumbling block” (Leviticus 19:14), for the descendants of Noah were not warned about this; and as for us, we find no prohibition in causing such association.

notes.he: שלא תבקש בפיך שישבע לך בעבודה זרה שלו:
notes.en: “Neither let it be heard out of your mouth”: that you not ask with your mouth that he swear to you by his idol.

messages.text: Rather, the tanna taught that a sale to a gentile is not permitted, and the same is true for the case of a partnership. So too, the tanna taught that a sale to a gentile is prohibited, and the same is true for a case of receivership.

notes.he: אינו רשאי והוא הדין לכולהו:
notes.en: It taught that a sale: is not permitted, and the same is true for all of them.

notes.dh: אלא תנא במכירה אע"פ שאינו רשאי וה"ה לשותפות
notes.he: דאינו רשאי להשתתף לו וה"ה בקבלנות דאינו רשאי ליתן לו בהמה בקבלנות דהמוכר בהמה לעובר דאסור לרבנן:
notes.en: Rather, it teaches regarding a sale “although he is not permitted,” and the same is true for partnership: that he is not permitted to enter a partnership with him; and the same is true for receivership, that he is not permitted to give him an animal in receivership, since according to the Rabbis one who sells an animal for its fetus is prohibited.

messages.text: And what is different about the case of selling that the tanna cited the prohibition specifically in that case?

notes.he: בה אינו רשאי ולא נקטיה בחדא מהנך:
notes.en: And what is different about a sale, that it cited: “he is not permitted” regarding it, and did not cite it with one of these others?

messages.text: That the primary prohibition is that of selling the animal to a gentile.

notes.he: עיקר איסורא הויא מכירת בהמה:
notes.en: That the primary prohibition is a sale: the primary prohibition is the sale of an animal.

notes.he: פרש"י דעיקר איסור הוא המכירה משמע שרוצה לומר שעיקר האיסור הוא המכירה וקשה הא שותפות לא מיתסר משום מכירה אלא כדאבוה דשמואל וצ"ל עיקר איסור הפשוט הוא מכירה כדתנן פרק קמא דמס' ע"ז (דף יד:):
notes.en: That the primary one is a sale: Rashi explained that the primary prohibition is the sale, meaning that he wants to say the primary prohibition is the sale. But it is difficult: partnership is not prohibited because of a sale, but because of what Shmuel’s father said. One must say: the primary, straightforward prohibition is a sale, as we learned in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (14b).

notes.he: דגבי מכירה קתני אע"פ שאינו רשאי דעיקר איסורא במכירה היא להכי תנא בה דאינו רשאי וה"ה לכולהו:
notes.en: And what is different about a sale, that it chose it: that regarding a sale it teaches “although he is not permitted”? Because the primary prohibition is in a sale; therefore it teaches regarding it that he is not permitted, and the same is true for all of them.

messages.text: Come and hear a resolution to the dilemma of whether selling an animal to a gentile with regard to the rights to its fetuses is permitted from a baraita:

In the case of one who receives an animal from a gentile to care for and receives a portion of the offspring in exchange for his work, and it gave birth to a firstborn, they assess its value, and the Jew gives half of its value to the priest to redeem his portion, which is considered to have the sanctity of a firstborn. And in the case of one who gives the gentile an animal in receivership even though he is not permitted to do so, the Sages penalize him by requiring that he purchase the gentile’s portion of the animal for up to ten times its value, and he gives all of its value to the priest.
As long as the ownership of the gentile is involved, in that he possesses at least partial ownership of the mother or the fetus, the animal is exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn.

notes.he: שיד העובד כוכבים באמצע שיש לו שום חלק בה:
notes.en: [As long as] the gentile’s hand is in the middle: that he has some share in it.

messages.text: Continues on 3a: the Gemara asks whether this baraita, in prohibiting receivership, is referring to the animal itself.
